title: Gut microbiota from twins discordant for obesity modulate metabolism in mice

claims.title: Donor population
claims.detail: The study used fecal microbiota samples from adult female twin pairs discordant for obesity.

claims.title: Recipient model
claims.detail: Fecal microbiota from the human donors were transplanted into germ-free mice.

claims.title: Diet condition
claims.detail: Recipient mice were maintained under controlled diet conditions in the gnotobiotic mouse experiment.

claims.title: Adiposity outcome
claims.detail: Mice receiving microbiota from obese co-twins developed greater adiposity-related phenotypes than mice receiving microbiota from lean co-twins.

claims.title: Cohousing result
claims.detail: When mice harboring obese-twin microbiota were co-housed with mice harboring lean-twin microbiota, members of the lean-donor microbiota could invade the obese-recipient communities.

claims.title: Diet-dependent invasion result
claims.detail: The invasion of lean-associated bacterial taxa and the associated metabolic phenotype depended on diet composition in the experiment.

title: An obesity-associated gut microbiome with increased capacity for energy harvest

claims.title: Mouse microbiome comparison
claims.detail: The study compared the distal gut microbiota of genetically obese mice and lean littermates.

claims.title: Dominant bacterial divisions
claims.detail: The authors reported differences in the relative abundance of dominant gut bacterial divisions between obese and lean animals.

claims.title: Energy harvest capacity
claims.detail: Metagenomic and biochemical analyses indicated that the obesity-associated microbiome had increased capacity for energy harvest from the diet.

claims.title: Human observation
claims.detail: The paper reported gut microbiome differences between obese and lean human volunteers.

claims.title: Germ-free mouse colonization
claims.detail: Colonization of germ-free mice with microbiota from obese donors produced greater increases in body fat than colonization with microbiota from lean donors.

title: Diet-microbiota interactions as moderators of human metabolism

claims.title: Diet-microbiota interaction
claims.detail: The review describes diet and gut microbiota as interacting factors in human metabolism.

claims.title: Diet shapes microbial composition
claims.detail: The review discusses evidence that dietary composition can alter gut microbial community structure and function.

claims.title: Microbial metabolism of diet-derived substrates
claims.detail: The review describes microbial metabolism of dietary substrates into metabolites relevant to host physiology.

claims.title: Host metabolic outcomes
claims.detail: The review discusses links between diet-microbiota interactions and host metabolic outcomes.

claims.title: Need for mechanistic understanding
claims.detail: The review emphasizes the need to understand mechanisms connecting diet, microbiota, microbial metabolites, and host metabolism.

title: Human genetics shape the gut microbiome

claims.title: Twin study design
claims.detail: The study analyzed gut microbiome data from monozygotic and dizygotic twin pairs.

claims.title: Heritable taxa
claims.detail: The authors identified microbial taxa whose abundance showed evidence of host genetic influence.

claims.title: Christensenellaceae heritability
claims.detail: The family Christensenellaceae was reported as one of the most heritable taxa in the study.

claims.title: Association with leanness
claims.detail: Christensenellaceae abundance was associated with a lean host phenotype in the reported data.

claims.title: Mouse transplantation test
claims.detail: The paper included a mouse experiment involving Christensenella minuta in a microbiota transplantation context.

claims.title: Microbiome-host genetics relation
claims.detail: The study concluded that host genetic variation contributes to variation in human gut microbiome composition.

title: Transkingdom control of microbiota diurnal oscillations promotes metabolic homeostasis

claims.title: Diurnal microbiota oscillations
claims.detail: The study reported diurnal oscillations in gut microbiota composition and function.

claims.title: Feeding rhythm link
claims.detail: The paper linked microbiota oscillations to host feeding rhythms.

claims.title: Host circadian disruption
claims.detail: Disruption of host circadian rhythms altered microbiota rhythmicity in the reported experiments.

claims.title: Metabolic phenotype
claims.detail: The study reported metabolic consequences associated with disruption of microbiota diurnal oscillations.

claims.title: Transfer experiment
claims.detail: The paper included microbiota transfer experiments connecting disrupted rhythmicity with metabolic phenotypes in recipient mice.

title: Microbial regulation of organismal energy homeostasis

claims.title: Energy homeostasis review
claims.detail: The review discusses ways in which gut microorganisms participate in organismal energy homeostasis.

claims.title: Microbial metabolites
claims.detail: The review discusses microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids and bile-acid-related pathways, in relation to host metabolism.

claims.title: Host-microbe signaling
claims.detail: The review describes host-microbe signaling pathways relevant to metabolic regulation.

title: Gut microbiota in human metabolic health and disease

claims.title: Human metabolic health review
claims.detail: The review summarizes associations between gut microbiota and human metabolic health and disease.

claims.title: Obesity and metabolic disease
claims.detail: The review discusses microbiome features reported in obesity and related metabolic disorders.

claims.title: Diet and medication effects
claims.detail: The review discusses diet, medication, and environmental factors as contributors to microbiome variation.

claims.title: Human intervention evidence
claims.detail: The review discusses human intervention studies targeting the gut microbiota in metabolic disease contexts.

claims.title: Individual variation
claims.detail: The review describes substantial inter-individual variation in microbiome composition and metabolic responses.

title: Gut microbiome and health: mechanistic insights

claims.title: Mechanistic review
claims.detail: The review discusses mechanistic links between the gut microbiome and host health.

claims.title: Microbial products
claims.detail: The review discusses microbial products and metabolites as mediators of host-microbiome interactions.

claims.title: Host context
claims.detail: The review discusses host context, diet, and environment as factors shaping microbiome-health relationships.

claims.title: Translation to interventions
claims.detail: The review discusses challenges and opportunities in translating microbiome mechanisms into interventions.
